title: Electronics — Chapter 2: DFM, Not Just Another Acronym

questions.question: Why did Etch-O-Matronic put Ian’s job on hold for trace width/spacing?
options: The CAM department rejected automated defaults that made 1 mil traces incompatible with process capability.
The credit card was declined before any CAM review started on the Gerber package for real production programs.
Otto deleted the design rules file during orientation and the fab refused unsigned jobs for real production programs.
Old Bob required every board to use only silk-screen artwork with no copper at all for real production programs.
questions.explanation: TRACE WIDTH AND SPACING INCOMPATABLE WITH OUR PROCESSING CAPABILITY

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design

questions.question: Old Bob’s point about “software allowed 1 mil traces” is best summarized as:
options: If the layout tool permits a geometry, the fab process can always etch and plate it reliably.
Tool permission is not process capability — choose trace width for performance and DFM.
One mil traces are mandatory for every avionics board regardless of the fab process for real production programs.
Defaults are always safer than talking to a manufacturing engineer about capability for real production programs.

questions.question: A bare board passed fab DFM but assembly put the job on hold. What did Old Bob explain?
options: Fab DFM and assembly DFA are identical, so the hold must be a shipping error only.
The finished bare PCB is a component; assembly quality is outside the fabricator’s scope.
The fab must reflow every connector before the board leaves the etch line for real production programs.
Assembly holds only happen when the BOM lists cake from the cafeteria menu for real production programs.
questions.explanation: It is the fabricator’s job to create a quality component

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: It is the fabricator’s job to create a quality component

questions.question: Which lesson does Ian’s checklist emphasize about CAD defaults?
options: Trust default software settings because automation equals manufacturability.
Do not trust default software settings — understand how to optimize them.
Disable all design-rule checks so CAM never sends disposition emails.
Set every trace to one mil so the fab can always fatten them later for real production programs.
questions.explanation: Do not trust default software settings to design your PCB

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Do not trust default software settings to design your PCB

questions.question: Before sending files for fabrication and assembly, the chapter urges you to:
options: Skip supplier contact until after the first scrap lot arrives.
Establish manufacturing contacts/mentors and use free DFM checks.
Publish Gerbers publicly so random fabs can bid without NDAs.
Remove all tolerances so CAM has maximum creative freedom.
questions.explanation: take advantage of free DFM checks before the design is sent

options: Only “How much did the Quickie-Cheapo fab charge per square inch?”
Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How across the manufacturing flow.
Only the cafeteria menu options available during an all-nighter.
Which star rating to click when choosing the next fab vendor.

questions.question: From a manufacturing perspective (High-Speed guide), impractical early design decisions:
options: Are wiped out automatically by any fab’s free online DFM button for real production programs.
Get baked into prototypes, stay through the lifecycle, and raise defect/cost risk.
Only matter for hobby boards and never for production avionics for real production programs.
Are fixed by increasing the public star rating of the chosen fab for real production programs.
